title: Short Stuff: Honorary Degrees
summary: Short Stuff episode on honorary degrees. The hosts explain that some universities (UVA, MIT, Stanford, Cornell) do not grant them, recounting William Barton Rogers's objection and Thomas Jefferson's ban despite Jefferson accepting a Harvard honorary doctorate. They describe the origins at Oxford with a fifteenth-century bishop named Lionel, King Charles I handing out 350 Oxford doctorates in one year, and the 19th-century devaluation of earned doctorates by mass honorary awards. They discuss why schools give them (donors, celebrity draw, inspiring graduates), how selection and invitations work, Florida Atlantic University's strict rules against using the title, Warren Throckmorton's survey of university policies, and rescinded honorary degrees such as Bill Cosby's, Jimmy Savile's, Oscar Pistorius's, and Donald Trump's. Ben Franklin is mentioned as a user of his Oxford and St. Andrews degrees.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode on honorary degrees during graduation season, joking about their own self-proclaimed doctorates.

segments.title: Universities that refuse honorary degrees
segments.summary: The hosts note that UVA, MIT, Stanford and Cornell do not give honorary degrees. MIT founder William Barton Rogers, a UVA graduate, criticized them, and Thomas Jefferson, UVA's founder, banned them yet accepted a Harvard honorary doctorate.

segments.title: Why honorary degrees are given
segments.summary: Honorary degrees are used to reward donors, attract celebrities for graduation ceremonies, and recognize people whose values align with the university, which generates press.

segments.title: Origins at Oxford and King Charles I
segments.summary: The tradition began in Europe at Oxford, which gave an unrequested honorary doctorate to a fifteenth-century bishop named Lionel. King Charles I later handed out 350 Oxford doctorates in one year, to supporters of his court, an example of abuse.

segments.title: Nineteenth-century degree devaluation
segments.summary: By the nineteenth century, mass honorary awards lessened the value of earned doctorates. A Northeastern Dental Association president condemned the practice of unearned degrees as degrading. The problem eased once recipients stopped using the titles as if legitimate.

segments.title: Selecting honorary degree recipients and commencement speakers
segments.summary: Schools use boards to choose recipients, often starting a year ahead, and recipients are expected to attend and give strong commencement remarks. Celebrities and big donors are common choices.

segments.title: Title usage rules and rescinded degrees
segments.summary: Florida Atlantic University forbids recipients from using doctor titles. Warren Throckmorton surveyed university policies. Ben Franklin used his degrees. Several honorary degrees were rescinded, including those of Bill Cosby, Jimmy Savile, Oscar Pistorius and Donald Trump.

segments.title: Closing and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts mention a listener's note about Canadian honorary degrees, joke about being granted one, and close with the show credits.
